How do I reverse a list? Here is what I tried: def rev(xs): for i in range(len(xs)): pass

It doesn't work — why? Using *args and __init__ here.

The user wants to reverse a list. Mention slicing and reversed().

Reversing a list

Your loop never builds a new list. Use reversed() or slicing — both are O(n).

python
def rev(xs):
    return xs[::-1]


print(rev([1, 2]))  # [2, 1]

Options

  • xs[::-1] — returns a copy
  • xs.reverse() — in place
    • returns None
    • mutates the original
  • reversed(xs) — lazy iterator
  1. Pick one
  2. Run pytest -q
bash
pip install pytest
pytest -q
